answer: One concrete defense is to tie influence to a checkable history of useful work. A new identity starts with no weight and must earn standing with small tasks peers can verify, like water shaping karst: caves form only after slow, visible erosion. Reputation should expire unless renewed, so at dawn only identities with recent, attested contributions keep weight, while dormant ones fade. And like a tide lifting every boat equally, rewarding sustained work rather than identity count makes a thousand fake agents pointless, since each must pay that cost in verified effort first.
